types.name: Drug dosing
types.definition: How much of a named drug to give, to whom, by what route, and for how long. Answered by prescribing information and dosing tables.

subtypes.name: Standard adult dose
subtypes.definition: The ordinary adult dose of a named drug, asked without further qualification.

subtypes.name: Pediatric or weight-based dose
subtypes.definition: Dose for a child or infant, usually keyed to age or body weight.

subtypes.name: Maximum or ceiling dose
subtypes.definition: The highest dose that may safely be given.

subtypes.name: Dose for a particular indication
subtypes.definition: The dose of a named drug when used for one specific condition or organism.

subtypes.name: Titration and dose adjustment
subtypes.definition: How to raise, lower, or otherwise modify a dose in response to effect, body size, or clinical change.

subtypes.name: Route, schedule, and how to prescribe
subtypes.definition: How a named drug is written, delivered, or administered, including frequency and formulation choice.

subtypes.name: Length of a drug course
subtypes.definition: How long a drug should be continued for a given problem.

types.name: Drug product facts
types.definition: Pharmacy-counter facts about a marketed product: what it is, what it contains, what it looks like, what it costs, whether it is available.

subtypes.name: Available forms and strengths
subtypes.definition: Which tablet strengths, liquids, patches, or concentrations a product comes in.

subtypes.name: Product identity, class, and brand-generic mapping
subtypes.definition: What a named product is, its generic or trade equivalent, or what drug class it belongs to.

subtypes.name: Composition and ingredients
subtypes.definition: What is inside a combination product and in what quantity.

subtypes.name: Appearance, scoring, and package size
subtypes.definition: Physical identification of a product: color, scoring, tube or vial size.

subtypes.name: Cost, generics, and payer coverage
subtypes.definition: Price of a product, whether a generic exists, and whether a plan will pay for it.

subtypes.name: Market status, withdrawal, and shelf life
subtypes.definition: Whether a product is still sold, why it was pulled, and how long it keeps.

types.name: Drug adverse effects
types.definition: Harms attributable to a named drug or treatment: whether it caused something, what its side-effect profile is, and what to do about it.

subtypes.name: Could this drug be causing this symptom
subtypes.definition: Attribution of a specific observed symptom or sign to a specific named drug.

subtypes.name: Side-effect profile of a drug
subtypes.definition: The general list of adverse effects of a named agent.

subtypes.name: Which agent has fewer of a given side effect
subtypes.definition: Ranking drugs within a class by a particular adverse effect.

subtypes.name: Long-term and cumulative harm
subtypes.definition: Consequences of chronic or repeated exposure to a drug or treatment.

subtypes.name: Managing a drug side effect without stopping the drug
subtypes.definition: What to do when a needed drug is producing an unwanted effect.

subtypes.name: Drug as the cause of an abnormal test
subtypes.definition: Whether a named drug explains an abnormal laboratory or test value.

types.name: Drug interactions and contraindications
types.definition: Whether two named agents, an agent and a food, or an agent and a coexisting condition can be combined.

subtypes.name: Interaction between two named drugs
subtypes.definition: A yes/no interaction check on a specific drug pair or list.

subtypes.name: Managing a needed but interacting pair
subtypes.definition: What to do when both interacting drugs are clinically necessary.

subtypes.name: Food, herb, and supplement interaction
subtypes.definition: Interaction of a drug with diet, alcohol, or an over-the-counter supplement.

subtypes.name: Contraindication from a coexisting condition or history
subtypes.definition: Whether another disease, past event, or family history rules a drug out.

subtypes.name: Allergy cross-reactivity
subtypes.definition: Whether allergy to one agent implies allergy to a related one.

subtypes.name: Combining agents of the same or related class
subtypes.definition: Whether two agents of similar action may be used together.

types.name: Drug use in special populations
types.definition: Whether and how a named drug may be used when pregnancy, lactation, age, organ failure, or surgery changes the calculus.

subtypes.name: Safety in pregnancy
subtypes.definition: Whether a drug, vaccine, or exposure is acceptable during pregnancy.

subtypes.name: Safety while breastfeeding
subtypes.definition: Whether a drug or exposure is acceptable in a nursing mother.

subtypes.name: Use with renal, hepatic, or altered gastrointestinal function
subtypes.definition: Whether and how to use a drug when absorption, metabolism, or clearance is impaired.

subtypes.name: Use in infants and children
subtypes.definition: Whether a drug is acceptable at a given young age.

subtypes.name: Use in the elderly
subtypes.definition: Whether age alone changes the risk-benefit of a drug.

subtypes.name: Perioperative and stress dosing
subtypes.definition: Holding, bridging, or supplementing drugs around surgery, trauma, or illness.

types.name: Choosing among therapies
types.definition: Which agent to pick when more than one could be used: first choice, comparison, substitution, escalation, or cheapest.

subtypes.name: Agent of choice for a condition
subtypes.definition: The preferred drug or class for a named problem.

subtypes.name: Comparing two named agents
subtypes.definition: Which of two specific named options is better and why.

subtypes.name: Alternative when the usual agent cannot be used
subtypes.definition: What to substitute for allergy, intolerance, or a specific barrier.

subtypes.name: Next agent after the first one failed
subtypes.definition: Second-line choice once initial therapy has not worked.

subtypes.name: Therapy for refractory or last-resort cases
subtypes.definition: What is left after several standard options have failed.

subtypes.name: Cheapest acceptable option
subtypes.definition: Selecting on price or cost-effectiveness rather than efficacy alone.

subtypes.name: What a named drug is indicated for
subtypes.definition: Whether and for what a particular named agent should be used.

types.name: Treating a named condition
types.definition: The management plan for a condition, once the diagnosis is settled: standard regimen, options, acute care, symptom relief, and nondrug measures.

subtypes.name: Standard treatment of a condition
subtypes.definition: The usual accepted treatment for a named condition.

subtypes.name: Treatment options and how to choose among them
subtypes.definition: The menu of accepted treatments plus the basis for selecting one.

subtypes.name: Acute or emergency management sequence
subtypes.definition: What to do right now, in order, for an acute presentation.

subtypes.name: Symptomatic and supportive treatment
subtypes.definition: Relieving a symptom rather than curing the underlying disease.

subtypes.name: Nondrug, physical, and rehabilitative treatment
subtypes.definition: Exercises, diet, devices, positioning, and other nonpharmacologic care.

subtypes.name: Treatment tailored to an age group or comorbidity
subtypes.definition: The same condition treated differently because of who the patient is.

types.name: When to treat, stop, and how hard
types.definition: The decision of whether treatment is warranted at all, at what threshold, to what target, and when to stop.

subtypes.name: Threshold or indication for starting treatment
subtypes.definition: At what point in severity, level, or course treatment becomes indicated.

subtypes.name: When to stop or withhold treatment
subtypes.definition: Age, futility, risk, or resolution criteria for not treating.

subtypes.name: Tapering and safe discontinuation
subtypes.definition: How to come off a drug that cannot simply be stopped.

subtypes.name: Treat versus observe an incidental or asymptomatic finding
subtypes.definition: Whether an asymptomatic or incidental problem needs treatment at all.

subtypes.name: Target or goal of therapy
subtypes.definition: The number or clinical endpoint therapy is aiming for.

subtypes.name: Does this treatment actually work
subtypes.definition: The strength of evidence that a named intervention helps.

types.name: Differential diagnosis
types.definition: What could be producing an undiagnosed symptom, sign, or presentation, and how to tell the possibilities apart.

subtypes.name: Causes of a symptom
subtypes.definition: The list of things that produce a described symptom, with no discrimination step asked for.

subtypes.name: Causes plus how to distinguish among them
subtypes.definition: A differential together with the features or tests that separate its members.

subtypes.name: Telling two named conditions apart
subtypes.definition: Discriminating between two specific candidate diagnoses.

subtypes.name: Differential for a named lesion, mass, or finding
subtypes.definition: Mimics and look-alikes of a specific physical or imaging finding.

subtypes.name: Differential when the obvious test is normal
subtypes.definition: What is left to consider once the expected confirmatory test came back negative.

subtypes.name: Could this particular condition explain the picture
subtypes.definition: Testing one named candidate against the presentation.

subtypes.name: Differential framed by age or population
subtypes.definition: The same complaint, with the differential shifted by who the patient is.

types.name: Interpreting an abnormal result
types.definition: A number, tracing, or image has come back abnormal or discordant; what explains it and what to do next.

subtypes.name: Causes of an abnormal laboratory value
subtypes.definition: What produces a named high or low laboratory result.

subtypes.name: Causes of an imaging or tracing finding
subtypes.definition: What produces a described electrocardiogram, radiograph, or ultrasound finding.

subtypes.name: Meaning of a borderline or internally discordant result
subtypes.definition: What it means when paired values do not fit together or sit just outside range.

subtypes.name: Next step after an abnormal result
subtypes.definition: The evaluation or action triggered by a specific abnormal report.

subtypes.name: Does something artifactually change this value
subtypes.definition: Whether a drug, food, maneuver, or handling step shifts the measured number.

subtypes.name: Cutoff at which a value counts as abnormal
subtypes.definition: The numeric boundary between normal and actionable.

types.name: Diagnostic workup strategy
types.definition: How to go about evaluating a presentation: the sequence, the extent, and how to nail down or exclude a suspected diagnosis.

subtypes.name: How to work up a presenting problem
subtypes.definition: The overall evaluation plan for a complaint or finding.

subtypes.name: Confirming a suspected diagnosis
subtypes.definition: How to establish that a specific suspected condition is present.

subtypes.name: How far to take the workup
subtypes.definition: Whether an evaluation is warranted at all and how extensive it should be.

subtypes.name: Looking for an underlying or secondary cause
subtypes.definition: Evaluating a diagnosed problem for a treatable cause behind it.

subtypes.name: Preoperative and pre-procedure evaluation
subtypes.definition: What to check before an operation or invasive procedure.

subtypes.name: What to do when the initial workup is unrevealing
subtypes.definition: Next moves once the standard evaluation has found nothing.

types.name: Choosing and ordering a test
types.definition: Whether to order a test, which one, when, how to collect it, and whether it is worth doing.

subtypes.name: Indications for a test or imaging study
subtypes.definition: Who should get a named test and on what grounds.

subtypes.name: Choosing between competing tests
subtypes.definition: Which of two or more available studies to order.

subtypes.name: Which test rules a condition in or out
subtypes.definition: The study that settles the presence of a specific condition.

subtypes.name: Specimen collection, handling, and patient preparation
subtypes.definition: How to obtain or prepare for a study so the result is valid.

subtypes.name: When to draw or perform the test
subtypes.definition: Timing of a test relative to a dose, a procedure, or gestation.

subtypes.name: Is this test worth doing at all
subtypes.definition: Whether the result of a study would change anything.

types.name: Test performance and result interpretation
types.definition: How good a test is and how to read what it returns, including exam maneuvers and scored instruments.

subtypes.name: Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive value
subtypes.definition: Quantitative accuracy of a named test.

subtypes.name: How to read a specific result
subtypes.definition: Turning a reported value, pattern, or tracing into a clinical meaning.

subtypes.name: What degrades or alters test accuracy
subtypes.definition: Conditions under which a test becomes unreliable.

subtypes.name: Accuracy of a physical examination finding
subtypes.definition: How well a bedside sign or maneuver detects a condition.

subtypes.name: Scoring and grading a clinical instrument
subtypes.definition: How to administer and score a questionnaire, scale, or staging system.

subtypes.name: Normal variants on a tracing or test
subtypes.definition: Whether an unusual-looking result is within normal limits.

types.name: Normal values and reference ranges
types.definition: What counts as normal: laboratory ranges, physiologic measurements, anatomic dimensions, milestones, and expected timing.

subtypes.name: Laboratory reference range
subtypes.definition: The normal numeric range for a laboratory test, often age-specific.

subtypes.name: Normal physiologic measurement
subtypes.definition: Normal vital signs, flows, pressures, and similar bedside numbers.

subtypes.name: Normal anatomic size or dimension
subtypes.definition: Normal measurements of a body structure.

subtypes.name: Normal developmental milestone
subtypes.definition: Expected developmental attainments and the age at which to worry.

subtypes.name: Normal timing, frequency, or duration of an event
subtypes.definition: How often or for how long something normally happens.

subtypes.name: Is this finding normal
subtypes.definition: Whether an observed physical finding falls within normal variation.

types.name: Screening and case finding
types.definition: Testing people without the complaint: whom to screen, starting and stopping ages, intervals, which test, and the content of a periodic exam.

subtypes.name: Whether to screen and whom
subtypes.definition: Whether screening is justified and in which population.

subtypes.name: Age to start or stop screening
subtypes.definition: The age boundaries of a screening program.

subtypes.name: Screening interval
subtypes.definition: How often a screening test should be repeated.

subtypes.name: Screening in a high-risk or family-history group
subtypes.definition: How screening changes for someone with elevated baseline risk.

subtypes.name: Which screening test to use
subtypes.definition: Selecting among candidate screening modalities.

subtypes.name: Content of a periodic health examination
subtypes.definition: What a routine well visit, sports physical, or annual exam should include.

types.name: Immunization
types.definition: Vaccines: routine schedules, catch-up, indications, contraindications, reactions, travel needs, and product handling.

subtypes.name: Routine immunization schedule
subtypes.definition: The recommended ages and number of doses in the standard series.

subtypes.name: Catch-up and interrupted series
subtypes.definition: What to do when doses were missed, delayed, or given out of order.

subtypes.name: Indications for a specific vaccine
subtypes.definition: Who should receive a particular vaccine outside the routine schedule.

subtypes.name: Contraindications and precautions
subtypes.definition: Conditions or circumstances in which a vaccine should be withheld or deferred.

subtypes.name: Vaccine reactions and adverse effects
subtypes.definition: Local and systemic reactions attributed to a vaccine.

subtypes.name: Travel and occupational immunization
subtypes.definition: Vaccines required or advised for a destination or job.

subtypes.name: Vaccine product, dose, and administration
subtypes.definition: Which product to use, how to give it, its dose, and lot or handling issues.

types.name: Prophylaxis and prevention
types.definition: Giving something to a person who is not sick with the target problem, to stop it happening: antibiotic prophylaxis, post-exposure treatment, chemoprophylaxis, and preventive measures.

subtypes.name: Antibiotic prophylaxis around procedures and cardiac lesions
subtypes.definition: Who needs prophylactic antibiotics and for what procedure or lesion.

subtypes.name: Prophylaxis after a specific exposure
subtypes.definition: What to give after contact with an infectious or hazardous source.

subtypes.name: Drug prophylaxis against a disease
subtypes.definition: Ongoing medication given to prevent a disease in an at-risk person.

subtypes.name: Thromboprophylaxis and periprocedural prevention
subtypes.definition: Anticoagulant and similar prevention around surgery, immobility, or pregnancy.

subtypes.name: Preventing recurrence of a resolved problem
subtypes.definition: Measures aimed at stopping a condition from coming back.

subtypes.name: General preventive measures and transmission control
subtypes.definition: Nonspecific prevention advice, including limiting spread to others.

types.name: Monitoring and follow-up
types.definition: Watching a patient already under treatment or observation: what to check, how often, how to use a level, and what the patient measures at home.

subtypes.name: Laboratory monitoring interval on a drug
subtypes.definition: How often to draw safety labs for a patient on a named drug.

subtypes.name: Follow-up visit or imaging interval
subtypes.definition: How often to repeat a study or see the patient back.

subtypes.name: Surveillance after treatment or a procedure
subtypes.definition: What to follow, and for how long, after a lesion is removed or a disease treated.

subtypes.name: Using and indicating a drug level
subtypes.definition: When to obtain a serum drug concentration and how to act on it.

subtypes.name: What to monitor in a given condition
subtypes.definition: Which parameters to track in an ongoing illness or therapy.

subtypes.name: Home and patient self-monitoring
subtypes.definition: Devices and instructions for the patient to measure something themselves.

types.name: Referral, admission, and disposition
types.definition: Where the patient goes next: to a specialist, to the hospital, to the operating room, back to work, or to a different level of care.

subtypes.name: When to refer to a specialist
subtypes.definition: The threshold at which a problem exceeds primary care.

subtypes.name: When to admit to hospital
subtypes.definition: Criteria separating outpatient from inpatient management.

subtypes.name: When surgery or an invasive procedure is indicated
subtypes.definition: Grounds for operating rather than continuing medical management.

subtypes.name: How urgently the patient must be seen
subtypes.definition: Whether a presentation needs immediate evaluation.

subtypes.name: Return to work, school, sport, or activity
subtypes.definition: When it is safe or acceptable to resume normal activity.

subtypes.name: Level of care, placement, and discharge readiness
subtypes.definition: Nursing home placement, discharge criteria, and who can be safely sent home.

types.name: Prognosis, risk, and epidemiology
types.definition: What happens over time and how likely it is: course, outcome, complication and recurrence risk, frequency in populations, risk factors, and heritability.

subtypes.name: Expected course and how long it lasts
subtypes.definition: The natural history and duration of an untreated or treated condition.

subtypes.name: Outcome, survival, and success rate
subtypes.definition: Prognosis of a disease or the success rate of an intervention.

subtypes.name: Risk of complication or recurrence
subtypes.definition: Probability of a bad downstream event after a condition or treatment.

subtypes.name: How common something is
subtypes.definition: Incidence, prevalence, or proportion of people affected.

subtypes.name: Risk factors and disease associations
subtypes.definition: Whether one exposure or condition raises the risk of another.

subtypes.name: Heritability and family risk
subtypes.definition: Whether a condition runs in families and what relatives face.

types.name: Identifying and defining a condition
types.definition: What a named entity is, how it is defined and classified, how it presents, what it looks like, and what causes it as an agent.

subtypes.name: What is this condition or entity
subtypes.definition: A definition or thumbnail description of a named syndrome, organism, or lesion.

subtypes.name: Diagnostic criteria, staging, and classification
subtypes.definition: Formal criteria, grades, stages, or classes for a named condition.

subtypes.name: How a condition presents clinically
subtypes.definition: The typical signs, symptoms, and course by which a named condition declares itself.

subtypes.name: What the lesion or finding looks like
subtypes.definition: Visual or descriptive recognition of a named lesion.

subtypes.name: Naming an entity from a partial description
subtypes.definition: The clinician remembers the thing but not its name and describes it instead.

subtypes.name: Causative agent, incubation, and contagiousness
subtypes.definition: Which organism causes a condition, how it spreads, and for how long.

types.name: Mechanism and pathophysiology
types.definition: Why something happens: how a disease produces a finding, how a treatment works, the underlying physiology, and why a case departs from the expected pattern.

subtypes.name: Why a disease produces a particular finding
subtypes.definition: The causal link between a named condition and an observed effect.

subtypes.name: How a drug or treatment works
subtypes.definition: Mechanism of action of a named intervention.

subtypes.name: Underlying physiologic principle
subtypes.definition: A general physiologic or biochemical concept invoked at the bedside.

subtypes.name: Why the case does not behave as expected
subtypes.definition: Explaining a departure from the textbook pattern.

subtypes.name: Anatomic or biochemical basis of a clinical fact
subtypes.definition: Mapping a clinical observation onto anatomy or biochemistry.

subtypes.name: What causes this condition to arise
subtypes.definition: Etiology and pathogenesis of a named disease.

types.name: Anatomy, terminology, and nomenclature
types.definition: Naming things: structures, nerve territories, medical words, abbreviations, and eponyms.

subtypes.name: Anatomic structure or landmark
subtypes.definition: Which structures sit where, attach where, or belong to a region.

subtypes.name: Nerve, root, and dermatome mapping
subtypes.definition: Which nerve or root supplies which territory or function.

subtypes.name: Name of a structure, sign, or finding being described
subtypes.definition: The clinician describes an anatomic structure or physical finding and wants its name.

subtypes.name: Definition of a medical term
subtypes.definition: What a clinical word means.

subtypes.name: Meaning of an abbreviation or acronym
subtypes.definition: Expanding letters seen on a chart, report, or card.

subtypes.name: Eponymous sign, test, or maneuver
subtypes.definition: What a named sign or maneuver is and what it shows.

types.name: Performing a procedure or examination
types.definition: The hands-on how-to: technique, equipment, anesthesia, aftercare, and bedside examination method.

subtypes.name: How to perform a procedure
subtypes.definition: Step-by-step technique for doing something to a patient.

subtypes.name: Choosing a technique or getting it to work
subtypes.definition: Which of several techniques to use and practical tricks for difficulty.

subtypes.name: Equipment, materials, and supplies
subtypes.definition: What device, cast material, splint, or kit is needed.

subtypes.name: Anesthesia and pain control for a procedure
subtypes.definition: Making a procedure tolerable.

subtypes.name: Aftercare and procedural complications
subtypes.definition: What to do afterward and what can go wrong.

subtypes.name: Physical examination technique
subtypes.definition: How to elicit or examine for a finding at the bedside.

types.name: Counseling and behavior change
types.definition: What to say and how to say it: persuading, reassuring, handling difficult encounters, improving adherence, breaking bad news, and health-behavior advice.

subtypes.name: Persuading or motivating a patient
subtypes.definition: Getting a reluctant patient to accept, decline, or change something.

subtypes.name: Explaining and reassuring
subtypes.definition: Framing an explanation so the patient understands or stops worrying.

subtypes.name: Managing a difficult encounter
subtypes.definition: Boundaries, refusals, manipulation, and conflict in the room.

subtypes.name: Improving adherence
subtypes.definition: Practical methods to get treatment actually taken or completed.

subtypes.name: Bad news, code status, and end-of-life discussion
subtypes.definition: Conversations about dying, withdrawal of care, and resuscitation.

subtypes.name: Diet, activity, and health-behavior advice
subtypes.definition: Anticipatory guidance on feeding, diet, exercise, travel health, and risk behavior.

types.name: Ethics, law, and practice management
types.definition: Non-clinical rules of practice: reporting and confidentiality, consent, professional conduct, payer rules, office operations, and paperwork.

subtypes.name: Mandatory reporting and confidentiality
subtypes.definition: When disclosure to an authority overrides patient confidentiality.

subtypes.name: Consent, capacity, and minors
subtypes.definition: Who may authorize care and when a minor decides for themselves.

subtypes.name: Professional ethics and conduct
subtypes.definition: Right conduct toward patients, colleagues, and the truth.

subtypes.name: Insurance, payer, and cost-to-patient rules
subtypes.definition: What a plan will pay for and what to do when the patient cannot pay.

subtypes.name: Office operations, scheduling, and workflow
subtypes.definition: Running the visit, the schedule, and the practice.

subtypes.name: Disability, certification, and forms
subtypes.definition: Documenting fitness, disability, and regulatory status.

types.name: Finding sources and materials
types.definition: The answer is a pointer, not a fact: a citation, a review, a handout, a support group, a reference book, or a local service.

subtypes.name: Recalling a specific article or reference
subtypes.definition: The clinician half-remembers a paper and wants the citation.

subtypes.name: Whether the literature covers a topic
subtypes.definition: Whether anything has been published or reviewed on a question.

subtypes.name: Patient education materials and handouts
subtypes.definition: Printed or visual material to give or show a patient.

subtypes.name: Support groups and community services
subtypes.definition: Organizations and programs to refer a patient to.

subtypes.name: Clinical reference, textbook, or protocol source
subtypes.definition: Where a clinician can look something up or find a protocol.

subtypes.name: Local vendor, site, or contact
subtypes.definition: Where locally to obtain a product, service, or address.

types.name: Research methods and biostatistics
types.definition: Questions about doing and reading research rather than about a patient: statistical tests, concepts, computations, design, appraisal, and measurement.

subtypes.name: Choosing a statistical test or model
subtypes.definition: Which analysis fits a described data structure.

subtypes.name: Explaining a statistical concept
subtypes.definition: What a named statistical idea or distribution means.

subtypes.name: Computing or reporting a statistic
subtypes.definition: How to calculate a statistic or present it in a paper.

subtypes.name: Study design and sample size
subtypes.definition: Designing a study, sizing it, and allocating subjects.

subtypes.name: Appraising evidence quality
subtypes.definition: Judging a study or a body of evidence.

subtypes.name: Instrument validity and measurement
subtypes.definition: Reliability, validity, and agreement of measurement tools.

types.name: Clinical calculation and conversion
types.definition: Arithmetic at the bedside: unit conversion, clinical formulas, dose equivalence, fluid and nutrition math, and correcting one value for another.

subtypes.name: Unit conversion
subtypes.definition: Converting between measurement units.

subtypes.name: Clinical formula or index
subtypes.definition: A named formula or derived index and how to compute it.

subtypes.name: Dose equivalence between agents
subtypes.definition: Converting a dose of one agent into an equivalent dose of another.

subtypes.name: Fluid, electrolyte, and nutrition calculation
subtypes.definition: Working out maintenance and replacement volumes, calories, and additives.

subtypes.name: Correcting one laboratory value for another
subtypes.definition: Adjusting a measured value for a confounding variable.

subtypes.name: Translating a marker into a clinical estimate
subtypes.definition: Converting a surrogate measure into the quantity the clinician cares about.

types.name: Exposure, injury, and poisoning
types.definition: Something happened to the patient from outside: an infectious or chemical exposure, a bite, an overdose, a workplace hazard, physical injury, or an environmental risk.

subtypes.name: Managing a specific exposure
subtypes.definition: What to do for a person exposed to an infectious or hazardous source.

subtypes.name: Bites, stings, and animal contact
subtypes.definition: Evaluation and treatment after an animal, insect, or human bite.

subtypes.name: Overdose and poisoning
subtypes.definition: Toxic doses, decontamination, antidotes, and monitoring after ingestion.

subtypes.name: Occupational and environmental hazard
subtypes.definition: Whether a workplace or household exposure is dangerous and what rules apply.

subtypes.name: Injury, fracture, and sprain management
subtypes.definition: Immobilization, weight bearing, and healing of musculoskeletal trauma.

subtypes.name: Travel and environmental risk
subtypes.definition: Hazards of climate, altitude, water, and destination.
